description:
Widened (Binary Handling's probe, develop 9089f7616): fz accepts ';' nowhere. The lexer makes Tok::Semi (src/parser/lexer.rs:1197) but no grammar rule consumes it, so the earlier premise 'wherever ; is already accepted' is wrong. All of these fail with parse/expected-token ... Semi:
- x = 1; IO.inspect(x) in a def body
- (x = 2; x)
- fn -> 3; 4 end
- if true do 5; IO.inspect(6) end
Elixir treats ';' as an end of expression exactly as a newline, so the fix is at that level: one rule, not one per construct. Fixtures for each form above on three paths.

Previous description: Elixir accepts fn -> a; b end (and fn x -> a; b end) with the semicolon separating two expressions of the body. fz refuses it with parse/expected-token ... Semi. Found while writing a spawned-process probe for fz-sc8.61; rewritten with newlines as a workaround in the probe only. Deviation from Elixir surface syntax; fix in the parser's block-body rule wherever ; is already accepted between expressions.

comments.text: Another instance (Optimize, 2026-11-19): fn -> a; b end rejected; Elixir accepts.

title: A semicolon separates expressions wherever a newline does
